'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
***[[Ukrainian forces]] retreat from [[Urozhaine, Donetsk Oblast|Urozhaine]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/ukraine-urozhaine-donetsk-map-army-b2582070.html (''The Independent'')]
***The [[Russia|Russian]] [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Ministry of Defence]] announces that [[Russian Armed Forces|its troops]] captured the village of [[Yurivka, Bakhmut Raion, Donetsk Oblast|Yuryivka]] in Donetsk Oblast. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2024/07/19/russian-army-says-captured-another-village-in-east-ukraine- (Al Arabiya)]
*[[2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement]]
**[[Bangladesh Police|Police]] in [[Dhaka]], [[Bangladesh]], ban all public rallies and protests in the city and impose a nationwide curfew, one day after protestors set fire to government buildings in the city. [https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2024/7/19/bangladesh-bans-rallies-as-violent-protests-spiral-out-of-control (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/communications-disrupted-bangladesh-amid-student-protests-2024-07-19/ (Reuters)]
**The [[government of Bangladesh]] cut off internet, mobile phone, and TV broadcast services in the country, instituting a [[media blackout]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20240719-deadly-clashes-between-police-and-students-during-protests-in-bangladesh (France 24)]
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**[[2024 Tel Aviv drone attack]]
***At least one person is killed and ten others are injured when a [[One-way attack drone|kamikaze drone]] strikes central [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]], near the [[Tel Aviv Branch Office of the Embassy of the United States|United States embassy]]. The [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] claim responsibility for the attack, and also issue an announcement that they will be providing details on a planned military operation on Tel Aviv soon. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog-july-19-2024/ (''The Times of Israel'')] [https://www.axios.com/2024/07/19/tel-aviv-israel-explosion (Axios)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Jadar mine|Jadar mining project]]
**The [[European Union]] and [[Serbia]] sign a deal to develop a [[lithium mining]] project and production chains for [[electric vehicle batteries|batteries for electric vehicles]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/eu-serbia-sign-key-lithium-deal/a-69712085 (DW)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Haitian crisis (2018–present)|Haitian crisis]]
**[[2024 Haiti boat fire]]
***At least 40 [[Haitians]] are killed and several others are injured when a boat travelling to the [[Turks and Caicos Islands]] catches fire. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2024/07/19/40-migrants-dead-after-boat-catches-fire-off-haiti (Al Arabiya)]
*Thirty-six people are rescued after fires break out onboard the [[São Tomé and Príncipe]]-flagged tanker ''Ceres I'' and [[Singapore]]-flagged tanker ''Hafnia Nile'' following a collision near [[Pedra Branca, Singapore]]. The remaining 26 ''Ceres I'' crew members remain onboard to conduct fire-fighting operations. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/search-and-rescue-for-crew-under-way-after-two-vessels-catch-fire-near-pedra-branca-mpa (''The Straits Times'')] [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/fire-search-and-rescue-underway-pedra-branca-helicopter-despatched-tankers-4490331 (CNA)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israeli allegations against UNRWA]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] announces the resumption of funding to the [[United Nations]] agency [[UNRWA]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/19/uk-to-resume-funding-to-un-agency-for-palestinian-refugees (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Palestine–European Union relations]]
**The [[European Commission]] announces [[Loan|loans]] and grants totalling €400 million (US$435.5 million) to the [[Palestinian Authority]] to prevent the government's financial collapse. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/fearing-palestinian-authority-collapse-eu-promises-435-mln-aid-2024-07-19/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in Belarus]]
**The [[Minsk]] Regional Court in [[Belarus]], in a secretive trial, sentences a [[Germany|German]] national Rico Krieger to death over alleged crimes including terrorism and [[mercenary]] activity. [https://www.dw.com/en/belarus-sentences-german-man-to-death-for-terrorism-rights-group/a-69716052 (DW)]
*[[Gaza humanitarian crisis (2023–present)|Gaza humanitarian crisis]], [[Societal breakdown in the Gaza Strip during the Israel–Hamas war]]
**The [[United Nations]] reports that "[[anarchy]]" and societal breakdown is expanding across the [[Gaza Strip]] due to [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] military destabilization, citing an increase in [[Looting|looting]] and [[Extrajudicial killing|extrajudicial killings]] of [[Palestinian Civil Police Force|police]] and [[Humanitarianism|humanitarian]] workers. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/un-rights-office-says-anarchy-spreading-gaza-2024-07-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[ICJ case on Israel's occupation of the Palestinian territories]], [[Israel and apartheid]]
**The [[International Court of Justice]] rules that [[Israel]]'s land annexation and [[Israeli settlements|settlement]] construction in [[East Jerusalem]] and the [[West Bank]] is unlawful, and demands an end to these practices "as soon as possible". The Court also rules that Israel's occupation in the West Bank amounts to [[crime of apartheid|apartheid]]. [https://apnews.com/article/icj-court-israel-palestinians-settlements-2d5178500c0410341b252335859f2316 (AP)] [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/icj-delivers-landmark-opinion-57-year-israeli-occupation (Middle East Eye)]
*A court in [[Yekaterinburg]], [[Russia]], convicts [[United States|American]] journalist [[Evan Gershkovich]] of spying and sentences him to 16 years in prison. [https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/19/media/evan-gershkovich-espionage-trial-verdict-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam|Communist Party general secretary]] and paramount leader of [[Vietnam]] [[Nguyễn Phú Trọng]] dies at the age of 80, and is succeeded on an acting basis by [[President of Vietnam|President]] [[Tô Lâm]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c51y3r09zr2o (BBC News)]
*[[Pakistan]]i [[National Counter Terrorism Authority|counter-terrorism authorities]] arrest [[Amin al-Haq]], a high-ranking member of [[Al-Qaeda]] and a close confidant of [[Osama bin Laden]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/pakistan/bin-laden-and-al-qaeda-associate-amin-ul-haq-arrested-by-pakistan/articleshow/111860921.cms (''Times of India'')]
*A [[Tunisia]]n court sentences opposition party leader {{Ill|Lotfi Mraïhi|fr}}, a potential presidential candidate, to eight months in prison on a charge of [[vote buying]], and also bans Mraïhi from running in presidential elections. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tunisian-court-jails-opposition-leader-bans-him-presidential-elections-2024-07-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Ukrainians|Ukrainian]] [[linguist]], [[Ukrainian nationalism|nationalist]] politician, and former [[People's Deputy of Ukraine|People's Deputy]] [[Iryna Farion]] is shot and killed in [[Lviv]], [[Ukraine]] by an unknown assailant. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/gunman-wounds-nationalist-former-parliamentarian-ukraines-lviv-2024-07-19/ (Reuters)]
*{{Ill|WazirX|hi|वज़ीरएक्स}}, an Indian [[cryptocurrency exchange]] owned by [[Binance]], announces a security breach in which $234 million USD in [[cryptocurrency]] was stolen, amounting to half of the platform's total assets. [https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/wazirx-suffers-security-breach-after-suspicious-230-million-transfer-124071800707_1.html (''Business Standard'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Tunisian presidential election]]
**Incumbent [[President of Tunisia|Tunisian president]] [[Kais Saied]] announces his candidacy for a second term. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/le-monde-africa/article/2024/07/19/tunisian-president-kais-saied-announces-bid-for-reelection-amidst-turbulent-first-term_6690836_124.html (''Le Monde'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2024 CrowdStrike incident]]
**Numerous organizations worldwide experience service disruptions due to a faulty [[CrowdStrike]] update resulting in [[blue screen of death|blue screens of death]] on [[Microsoft Windows]] computers. [https://www.theverge.com/2024/7/19/24201717/windows-bsod-crowdstrike-outage-issue (The Verge)]
**[[American Airlines]], [[Delta Air Lines]], and [[United Airlines]] order a temporary global [[ground stop]] of many of their flights in response to the widespread computer outages. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/american-airlines-issues-global-ground-stop-flights/story?id=112092372 (ABC News)]
